messages.subject: Re: Doubt in FindNextItem function in mirtCAT
parts:
On Thu, Oct 30, 2014 at 1:50 AM, Irshad Mujawar <irshadmuj...@gmail.com> wrote:


Hello Phil,

Prologue: extract.item is used in Drule funcion, a criteria of the next item selection. The code for Drule

Drule <- function(which_not_answered, possible_patterns, person, test, row_loc, method,
                  prior = FALSE){
    infos <- lapply(which_not_answered, function(x)
        FI(extract.item(test$mirt_object, x), Theta=person$thetas))
    crit <- lapply(infos, function(x, person) det(x + person$info_thetas), person=person)
    crit <- do.call(c, crit)
    crit
}


When you  apply the extract.item on an mirt object one of the outputs which get after using a prefix @ to the stored output.
For example:

nitems <- 50
itemnames <- paste0('Item.', 1:nitems)

a <- matrix(rlnorm(nitems, .2, .3))
d <- matrix(rnorm(nitems))
dat <- simdata(a, d, 1000, itemtype = 'dich')
colnames(dat) <- itemnames
mod <- mirt(dat, 2)


kk=extract2(mod,2)
> kk@fixed.design
     [,1]
[1,]    0

fixed.design is getting used below.


ProbTrace = function(x, Theta, useDesign = TRUE, ot=0){
  if(nrow(x@fixed.design) > 1L && useDesign)
    Theta <- cbind(x@fixed.design, Theta)
  P <- P.mirt(x@par, Theta=Theta, ot=ot)
  return(P)
}


In the above code of 'ProbTrace' function what does fixed.design stand for? Is it always 0?

It's used in other functions in the package to include fixed effect predictors. See ?mixemirt for examples.
 



I need to use findNextItem function without using mirt object or mirtCAT object for that sake. Because it is too big. I just need to only those values coming from mirt object which are getting used in findNextItem function.

What do you mean "it's too big"? The objects should be relatively small, even if your pool size is extremely large.

Phil

Hi Irshad,

It sounds like you are using the mirtCAT tools in a separate CAT implementation. I would hold off for now until I find the time to write better updating functions internally which can be exported for such a use. That way the consistency could be better controlled on my end, and the package development won't break your code. Cheers.

Phil

Hi Irshad,

I can't see those images for some reason, so it's difficult to really answer your Q. 

However, if you're asking why you can't just take the determinants of the test information and item information independently and add them together, think about how the information matrix looks for a single unidimensional item, and why it's determinant will always be 0. That should explain why you have to take the determinant of the sum rather than the sum of the determinants. Cheers.

Phil

Hello Phil,

Prologue: extract.item is used in Drule funcion, a criteria of the next item selection. The code for Drule

Drule <- function(which_not_answered, possible_patterns, person, test, row_loc, method,
                  prior = FALSE){
    infos <- lapply(which_not_answered, function(x)
        FI(extract.item(test$mirt_object, x), Theta=person$thetas))

When you  apply the extract.item on an mirt object one of the outputs which get after using a prefix @ to the stored output.
For example:

nitems <- 50
itemnames <- paste0('Item.', 1:nitems)

a <- matrix(rlnorm(nitems, .2, .3))
d <- matrix(rnorm(nitems))
dat <- simdata(a, d, 1000, itemtype = 'dich')
colnames(dat) <- itemnames
mod <- mirt(dat, 2)


kk=extract2(mod,2)
> kk@fixed.design
     [,1]
[1,]    0

fixed.design is getting used below.


ProbTrace = function(x, Theta, useDesign = TRUE, ot=0){
  if(nrow(x@fixed.design) > 1L && useDesign)
    Theta <- cbind(x@fixed.design, Theta)
  P <- P.mirt(x@par, Theta=Theta, ot=ot)
  return(P)
}


In the above code of 'ProbTrace' function what does fixed.design stand for? Is it always 0?

It's used in other functions in the package to include fixed effect predictors. See ?mixemirt for examples.
 



I need to use findNextItem function without using mirt object or mirtCAT object for that sake. Because it is too big. I just need to only those values coming from mirt object which are getting used in findNextItem function.

What do you mean "it's too big"? The objects should be relatively small, even if your pool size is extremely large.

Phil
